scope: All 28 active registered editorial lines screened after staging the required 1 November Global Macro. New Korean official customs release dated 1 Nov compared with 31 Oct NBS PMI, 30 Oct Eurostat/Treasury, 29 Oct BEA/ICI, 28 Oct World Bank, 14 Oct IEA, 2 Oct FAO and WHO recent outbreak/risk listings. No separate thematic item has a new primary-source causal result beyond macro or prior corpus. A screening is not proof that no other event occurred.

reviewed_lines.note: MT-GM-2026-11-01 staged EN/PT with official 1 Nov Korea October exports $115.28bn (+93.7% y/y), chips $56.44bn (+259.4%), crude import price +62.0% versus volume -6.3%, against China PMI 49.3; 14 end sources and 4 charts.
Korean merchandise surplus $42.50bn is goods trade, not net financial-account flows; US ICI money-market assets do not identify Korean investors. Weekly reconciliation belongs to 2/5.
Korean semiconductor concentration and energy-price burden are important but a single October trade release does not establish a persistent national structural transition or social outcomes.
Korean October customs and China PMI are relevant country evidence, not enough to replace canonical country-context dossiers without full stock/flow institutional analysis.
Korean chips $56.44bn and computers $5.85bn are trade receipts, not newly demonstrated AI capability or independently measured deployment. Weekly technology task owns capability stage.
No new verified utilization, energy efficiency, returns on AI datacenters or sustained output capacity; Korea electrical-equipment $1.99bn (+74%) is a sales signal, not commissioned power.
IEA Sept Hormuz 10.9 mb/d and OPEC 4 Oct required production contextualized. No 1 Nov physical route measurement or verified new armed escalation adopted as fact.
Korean export receipts do not reveal ownership, financing control or signed supplier contracts beyond existing HBM4 candidate; no new actor dossier.
Fed 28 Oct held 3.75–4.00%, ECB 29 Oct held deposit 2.50%, UST 30 Oct 10Y 4.94%; no Sunday trading close or 1 Nov central-bank decision invented.
OPEC+ 1 Nov meeting scheduled but not confirmed as completed at 05 BRT; 4 Oct official communiqué still last verified seven-country decision.
Korean trade surge and energy import costs are outcomes of markets, not proof of a newly implemented fiscal or industrial policy and its counterfactual effects.
High nominal chip receipts do not document a new monetary instrument, market design or operating experiment; avoid speculative digital-currency causal links.
Trade balance and equity valuations do not measure beneficial ownership or asset control; no new ownership-resolved monthly capital dataset.
No new globally comparable annual control/reserve/wealth stock census; Korean merchandise exports are flows, not ownership stock.
Korean MOTIR, Chinese NBS, Fed/ECB and IEA observed; no new verified mandate or institutional redesign beyond already reported decisions.
Korean exports to ASEAN $21.33bn (+128%) and EU $8.10bn (+56.4%) are bilateral/regional trade values, not evidence of a new integration treaty.
AI equipment export growth does not quantify employment displacement, household distribution or technological access; no independently measured social impact delta.

FAO Sep food index 136.0 (+1.5% m/m), next release 6 Nov; WB Oct food outlook is forecast. Korean agricultural-food exports $1.11bn (+11.6%) do not establish food affordability, pesticide exposure or nutrition outcomes.

Herd management, antimicrobial use/resistance, pesticide and chemical exposure screened against WHO/FAO/WOAH governance context; no newly validated comparative intervention or outbreak series to justify separate analysis.
Gulf oil route disruption treated as conditional mechanism using dated IEA estimates. No imminent major-power war claim or new deployment inferred from unverified reports.

WHO 30 Oct yellow-fever rapid-risk-assessment listing and 23 Oct Ebola outbreak require source-level verification; previously rejected Ebola thematic not duplicated or converted into new outbreak claim.
No new primary archival material for intellectual-history or historical-political economy work; current Korean trade statistics do not justify another historical essay.

Korea energy imports $16.49bn (+63.1%), crude import unit price +62.0% and physical volume -6.3%; electrical equipment exports $1.99bn (+74%) warrant Atlas discovery, not another article repeating macro.
No new primary verified election-law, fiscal or institutional decision with distinct cross-country consequences; prior Brazil election coverage remains separate.
Korean import cost and IEA Sept stocks do not establish new mineral-reserve certification, sovereign control or ownership transfer; Brazil rare-earth corpus not duplicated.
Korean transformers/cables export value points to demand, not installed grid megawatts, a binational electricity agreement or datacenter commissioning; no Itaipu-specific new primary action.
Korea destination trade China $26.98bn, US $24.90bn, ASEAN $21.33bn, Latin America -37% y/y; no independent 1 Nov freight throughput for new corridor assessment.
IEA Sep observed oil stocks -509 mb versus end-Feb, FAO Sep prices and Korean crude import bill examined; no harmonized current food/medical/mineral/energy reserve inventory.
